unit: Publication-level provisional audit. NOT 50 distinct writers and NOT labels for each contributor.
reading_scope: All 50 downloaded public About pages; selected leads and policy/role passages from up to three of the 266 seeded sampled posts per publication, with additional targeted passages where needed. Separate pilot texts cited where indicated. Not all 266 posts read cover to cover. Expanded review: twelve About pages revisited, 26 public texts read fully and thirteen additional texts reviewed through selected passages; see Substack_Unresolved_Alignment_Review.json.
codebook: Ideology describes demonstrated policy orientation or explicit public self-description. Coalition and expressed commitment are separate. Unknown is valid; calm, independent or nonpartisan branding is not evidence of ideological centrism. Issue-specific progressive positions do not imply economic-left positions. Historical conservative origins are not current policy scores. Confidence is holistic and some party/organization evidence is stronger than ideology evidence.

counts.description: Includes progressive, liberal and center-left editorial tendencies; some new classifications remain tentative and issue-specific.
Silver Bulletin: moderate/classical liberal with libertarian tendencies. This is a coarse working placement, not ideological neutrality or an exact midpoint.
The Weekly Dish, The Huckabee Post and Charlie Sykes’s To the Contrary. Sykes is an anti-Trump conservative; conservative policy identity and Republican voting are distinct.

counts.group: Conservative origins with current policy range unresolved
counts.description: Adam Kinzinger and Rick Wilson. These two were outside the twelve-publication expanded review; their earlier classifications are retained.
The Free Press, The Bulwark, The Contrarian and Racket News. Their original classifications are retained; mixed contributor positions are not automatically centrist.
HOWL: clearly Trump-critical insider reporting, but insufficient affirmative policy evidence for a broad left/center/right placement.

rows.rationale: The source explicitly describes political heterogeneity. Four sampled public texts are mostly technology and previews; they do not justify coding every contributor as right-wing or centrist.

A home for the politically homeless, organized around liberal democracy. Sample includes a Progressive editor and multiple distinct reporters; publication-level anti-Trump orientation does not identify each writer’s ideology.
The sampled account favors abortion rights and contrasts Democratic electoral gains with Republican extremism. The label is provisional, not inferred from anti-Trump criticism alone.
Resistance rhetoric and identification with Harris supporters accompany reporting. A named editorial network, not a single writer.

rows.ideology: Left / progressive; editorial tendency across contributors
rows.coalition: Anti-Trump; includes criticism of Democratic leadership from the left
rows.rationale: The larger public-text review includes affirmative economic-progressive advocacy for worker organizing and rejection of corporate influence, defenses of public healthcare coverage, and immigration analysis critical of restrictionism. This supports a broad progressive editorial tendency rather than merely an anti-Trump label. Zeteo publishes multiple authors and explicitly disclaims that each opinion is the organization’s own; do not assign every contributor the same ideology.
Contributors explicitly need not agree on issues. Profits support litigation against Trump; this distinguishes the hybrid organization from a generic newsroom.

rows.coalition: Critical of Trump and progressive orthodoxy; formal party commitment not established
rows.rationale: Silver directly calls himself a moderate liberal and favors individual rights, free speech, decentralized decision-making and markets. A later essay explicitly places this form of liberalism closer to the center than the left. For a coarse three-way description, center/moderate liberal is the best working category. This does not mean neutral reporting, an exact ideological midpoint, or absence of liberal issue positions. Coding Silver as center-left is a reasonable sensitivity rather than calling him progressive-left or Republican.
Favors an immigration path to citizenship; sampled tariff and aid criticism supplies additional policy context. Do not infer a formal party identity.
Author explicitly identifies the product as satirical news. Satirical targets suggest orientation, but fictional statements cannot be treated as factual endorsements.
Favorable Harris comparison and inequality/corporate-power framing support a progressive, Democratic-aligned interpretation. The newsletter also includes a collaborator and interviews.

rows.ideology: Center-left / liberal; civil-rights and labor emphasis
rows.rationale: The reviewed Labor Day essay rejects Reagan’s small-government economic program, affirms organized labor and civil-rights work, and urges electoral action. The poll-tax essay defends expansive voting access and objects to exclusionary requirements. This is substantive liberal framing, not simply a biography as an Obama appointee. A detailed economic platform remains unmeasured.

rows.coalition: Critical of both; no party pledge
rows.rationale: Criticizes legacy-media accounts while also discussing Trump’s excesses. Free-speech positions and anti-establishment reporting do not by themselves establish Republican loyalty or a fixed left-right location.

rows.ideology: Conservative Republican origins; current policy range unconfirmed
rows.rationale: Explicitly describes twelve years as a Republican congressman and loss of party ties after opposing Trump. Historical origins are recorded separately from current policy ideology.
rows.summary_group: Conservative origins with current policy range unresolved

rows.rationale: The separately reviewed pilot explicitly recommends incremental public health coverage, supply reform and Democratic coalition priorities. Supporting AOC for a committee role does not make the author a socialist.
Climate action, racial justice and democratic norms are positively valued. Team-authored pieces and staff changes require distinguishing Dan Rather from the Steady brand.

rows.ideology: Center-left / socially liberal civic analysis; provisional
rows.coalition: Nonpartisan civic brand; no formal party commitment established
rows.rationale: McMahon’s own public prose rejects firearm-worship arguments and asks that children not have access to guns, advocates a constitutional amendment limiting money in politics, and criticizes religious-political curriculum mandates. Together these support a tentative liberal-leaning/center-left editorial assessment. Independence and a calm tone are not the basis for this label. Fiscal policy and many other domains remain unmeasured. An independent gubernatorial guest’s self-description is not McMahon’s.
Judd Legum expressly identifies as progressive while stating that readers need not share his views. Former campaign employment is biographical evidence, not proof of present party obedience.

rows.publication: Hope for America with Heather Delaney Reese
rows.ideology: Center-left / liberal; social-protection and immigrant-rights emphasis
rows.rationale: The Social Security essay affirmatively defends social insurance and Medicaid against cuts paired with tax benefits for the wealthy. Immigration commentary rejects scapegoating and calls for taking Congress back. These give positive social-protection and rights positions beyond generalized anti-MAGA criticism.

rows.ideology: Left / progressive, with mixed contributor backgrounds
rows.rationale: Self-description is progressive independent media, featuring Lincoln Project talent. Do not give every former Republican contributor the publication’s progressive label.

rows.ideology: Center-left / moderate liberal; former Republican, Democratic-aligned
rows.coalition: Democratic-aligned anti-Trump; self-reported Democratic registration in a 2024 post
rows.rationale: Schmidt’s 2024 autobiographical post says he left the GOP in 2018 and registered as a Democrat in 2020; it does not verify his registration today. More substantively, his own writing opposes reproductive restrictions and discrimination against gay people, and condemns the transfer of resources from working families and healthcare to wealthy interests. A moderate-liberal/center-left working label fits this current editorial material better than either Republican-conservative or merely unknown. A detailed economic ideology is not established.
Democratic gains are presented favorably alongside criticism of MAGA institutional control. This provides coalition evidence more clearly than a comprehensive policy ideology.
Explicitly presents anti-LGBTQ bills failing as victories. A strong issue position does not establish loyalty to every Democratic politician or an economic ideology.

rows.coalition: Critical of both; no party pledge
rows.rationale: Criticism of gender-policy progressivism and Biden coexists with extensive criticism of Trump’s executive power and election conduct. About page institutionalizes an edited dissent section; email selection is not the same as open comments.
The separately reviewed pilot explicitly defends intentionally positive Biden coverage and identifies itself as commentary rather than journalism. Electoral mobilization is also explicit.
Former Obama adviser explicitly offers a newsletter for defeating Trump and MAGA. Party strategy is better identified than the precise degree of economic progressivism.
Explicitly seeks a progressive future and defeating Trump; a later sampled rant criticizes Democrats’ weak opposition. Party commitment does not mean absence of intra-party criticism.
About page explicitly describes a largely progressive audience and a cast of contributors. Article-level legal analysis should not be conflated with a formal party institution.

rows.ideology: Center-left / liberal; reproductive-rights and equal-protection emphasis
rows.rationale: Two longer public pieces explicitly favor reproductive autonomy and defend abortion access while criticizing restrictions and attacks on healthcare provision. This supplies substantive liberal editorial evidence missing from the initial short-video sample. Multiple authors and advocacy partners contribute; do not attribute every piece to Michael Popok. Medical or legal factual claims are not adjudicated by this ideology review.
About page praises the Democratic Party and Biden; articles solicit money and volunteering for Democratic candidates. Degree of left economic ideology remains less certain than party commitment.

rows.ideology: Center-left / socially liberal editorial framing; nonpartisan news brand
rows.coalition: Democratic-friendly coverage; formal party pledge not established
rows.rationale: The editor’s own introductions affirm reproductive-rights work and characterize abortion restrictions and their consequences critically. The outlet also gives space to pragmatic Democratic figures and maintains a fact-explanation mission. This supports a tentative center-left editorial tendency without equating a nonpartisan news brand with centrism or assigning it a party identity. Guest views and poll findings are not coded as the editor’s own.
Explicitly works to elect Democratic candidates and supplies daily political actions. This is an organizing product rather than a general news agency.
A named Raw Story/Really American network describes itself as a people-powered response to MAGA media ownership. Multiple staff and brand bylines make individual attribution difficult.

rows.publication: The Good in Us by Mary L. Trump
rows.rationale: Urges Democratic leadership not to concede to Republicans. Many sampled records have missing bylines, so Mary Trump’s author identity cannot be assumed for all texts.

rows.ideology: Conservative Republican origins; current policy range unconfirmed
rows.rationale: Explicitly rejects being a progressive or liberal, describes former Republican roots, and commits to fighting the current GOP. An important case where anti-Trump does not mean left.
rows.summary_group: Conservative origins with current policy range unresolved

rows.ideology: Center-left / pluralist liberal; cohosts have cross-cutting positions
rows.coalition: Democratic electoral preference with internal disagreement
rows.rationale: Beth Silvers explicitly rejects identifying her conversational moderation with centrist policy views, describes welcoming immigration and left/libertarian criminal-justice positions, and calls a Democratic midterm victory imperative. Sarah identifies herself as a Democrat in a separate transcript. This resolves the broad outlet tendency while preserving differences between the cohosts; a shared tone is not a shared point on every issue.
About page explicitly calls the creator left; sampled essay advocates supporting even conservative Democrats over Republicans to secure governing power.

rows.coalition: Anti-Trump; explicit Harris endorsement despite policy disagreements
rows.rationale: In an interview republished on his own newsletter, Sykes says his conservative principles have not changed and specifically retains disagreements over tax policy and student debt while endorsing Harris on democratic grounds. His own commentary situates this within a conservative anti-Trump coalition, with later criticism of MAGA and attention to Democratic moderation. This is a clearer current center-right/conservative case than the initial sampled excerpts showed. It is not pro-Trump.
Explicit progressive politics mission and talk-show identity; policy commentary plus songs, book excerpts and collaborators require genre separation.

rows.publication: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
rows.rationale: Explicitly attacks conservative politics, not just Trump personally. Insults and humorous labels are rhetorical style, not a numerical extremity scale.
Explicitly funds progressive voices and ideas. The Pod Save America brand includes many distinct authors and formats.

rows.ideology: Center-left / liberal; exact economic position provisional
rows.rationale: Explicit mission makes a positive case for liberalism. Liberalism is not automatically equivalent to a Democratic party commitment, nor does it put all writers at the same policy point.

rows.ideology: Insufficient policy evidence; strongly Trump-critical insider commentary
rows.coalition: Strongly Trump-critical; party commitment not established
rows.rationale: The expanded reading establishes an oppositional stance toward Trump’s authoritarian behavior and a focus on insider reporting, personality and elite power. It does not provide a sufficiently broad affirmative position on redistribution, healthcare, immigration or other domains to distinguish left, center or a dissident right. Criticism of Fauci’s celebrity or Trump’s war management is not a policy platform. Keep broad ideology unclassified rather than inventing centrism.

rows.coalition: Democratic-oriented electoral analysis; formal party identity not established
rows.rationale: The longer review combines explicit support for institutional reforms in the About page, an own-voice statement that Democrats should optimize their chances of winning, and a business/editorial account aligning the publication with evidence-based resistance to right-wing attacks on democracy. This supports a tentative center-left/liberal-democratic editorial placement. It is an inference about orientation, not a full policy score. Poll respondents’ preferences, projected Democratic wins and technical corrections are not themselves ideological evidence.

Additional sampled passage critiques punitive three-strikes policy and far-right claims; another defends Biden against a campaign attack. Current free-post coverage is sparse and most material is paid.

rows.ideology: Left / progressive on Palestine and foreign policy
rows.rationale: Explicit Palestinian-freedom mission and criticism of mainstream two-state rhetoric. It is a strong issue position, not a complete economic ideology or party identity.

rows.publication: The Left Hook with Wajahat Ali
rows.author_or_brand: THE LEFT HOOK with Wajahat Ali
rows.rationale: Condemns Biden’s Palestine policy while arguing Trump would be worse. Critical electoral support and policy disagreement must remain separate dimensions.

rows.coalition: Critical of both; no party pledge
rows.rationale: Compares Trump, Harris and RFK on health-care failures and corporate power; national-security reporting is highly critical of executive power. About page identifies KlipNews and a named editor, so this is no longer safely treated as a wholly solo operation.
Explicitly identifies as liberal news and commentary with roughly a dozen daily stories. Humor does not make the whole outlet fictional satire in the Borowitz sense.

Explicit anticipation of Trump’s second term and a Huck PAC donation appeal. Names a writing/editing team and Blue Diamond Media ownership; a brand byline cannot identify Mike Huckabee as every article’s actual author.
Explicit left-wing perspective; anti-war critique of Trump’s cabinet does not imply uncritical Democratic loyalty.

right_comment_coverage.coalition: Critical of both; no party pledge
right_comment_coverage.rationale: Criticism of gender-policy progressivism and Biden coexists with extensive criticism of Trump’s executive power and election conduct. About page institutionalizes an edited dissent section; email selection is not the same as open comments.

This is a clearer current center-right/conservative case than the initial sampled excerpts showed. It is not pro-Trump.

data_rule: Saved-source provisional classification only; expanded manual review of twelve previously unresolved publications. Other thirty-eight classifications retained. No model API, new scraping or live ideology reassessment. No independent human validation.
